business_problem: Humana needed to meet FHIR interoperability requirements and modernize patient-data delivery without rewriting decades-old core systems that store sensitive healthcare data for millions of members.
solution_summary: Humana implemented a cloud-native interoperability layer on MongoDB Atlas rather than trying to modernize its entire core platform at once. The team built a core data fabric that pulls records from legacy systems of record through multiple data pipelines, standardizes them in an operational data layer on Atlas, and stages claims and clinical data from disparate sources into one API-ready document store. Because the delivery model is API first and the FHIR standard uses RESTful protocols, Atlas became the fast-serving backbone for interoperable APIs that need consistent, low-latency access to patient information. Downstream, Humana partners with Microsoft Azure's FHIR-focused cloud storage solution to satisfy interoperability standards. The result is a two-tiered architecture that preserves legacy systems, accelerates FHIR rollout, and separates reusable healthcare data services from older transactional applications.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the standardized healthcare records that Humana stages from legacy systems for rapid, interoperable API access.

solution_components.name: FHIR APIs
solution_components.role: Expose the normalized claims and clinical data to interoperable healthcare consumers through RESTful interfaces.

data_flow: Claims and clinical data are pulled from Humana's legacy systems into a core data fabric, staged in MongoDB Atlas in a standardized format, served through FHIR APIs, and then exchanged with downstream interoperability services including Microsoft's FHIR-focused cloud storage solution.
integration_points: Microsoft Azure FHIR-focused cloud storage solution
business_outcome: Humana improved patient experience and bidirectional data exchange while meeting interoperability mandates, without a disruptive rip-and-replace of its legacy healthcare systems.
metrics: Humana's core platform came together over decades.
The systems are business-critical and hold the private healthcare data of millions of people.
The FHIR mandate, which started taking effect in 2020, aligns with Humana's corporate strategy.
architecture_clues: Humana uses a core data fabric and an operational data layer to shield legacy systems from direct interoperability demands.
Multiple data pipelines converge claims and clinical data into one standardized source in MongoDB.
The design is explicitly API first and cloud native.
evidence_quotes: Humana tackled this problem by building a core data fabric that had the ability to both provide data from their systems of record and make them available to support additional requirements.
The APIs within the FHIR standard are based on RESTful protocols, which fit perfectly into MongoDB's application data platform.
It had to be something that could serve data very fast.
As one of the first healthcare insurers to fully implement FHIR, Humana was able to start improving patient experiences right away by introducing real-time data integration.
